question.text:
Let's consider the interpretation $v$ where $v(p)=F, v(q)=T, v(r)=T$.

Does $v$ satisfy the following propositional formulas?

  1. $(p ightarrow eg q) \vee eg(r \wedge q)$
  2. $( eg p \vee eg q) ightarrow(p \vee eg r)$
  3. $ eg( eg p ightarrow eg q) \wedge r$
  4. $ eg( eg p ightarrow q \wedge eg r)$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Someone ate Ronaldo's cookies from his seat in the pavilion. There are three suspects: Messi, Mbappe and Haaland. Ofcourse, all three of them deny stealing. When forced to open their mouths, they say:

Messi: "Ronaldo knows Mbappe, but Haaland liked his cookies."
Mbappe: "I don't even know Ronaldo. Besides, I was on the pitch at that time."
Haaland: "I saw both Messi and Mbappe without Ronaldo in the pavilion at that time, one of them must have done it."

Assume that the two innocent men are telling the truth, but the guilty man may or may not be. Who ate the cookies? 

  1. Messi
  2. Mbappe
  3. Haaland
  4. Cannot be determined from the given statements
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
• p = "Roses are red"
  • q = "Violets are blue"

Which of the following are correct applications of De Morgan's Laws? (Select all that apply)

  1. ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q
  2. ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q
  3. ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q
  4. ¬(¬p ∧ ¬q) ≡ p ∨ q
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Statement 1 — Mathematician to student: "If a function is not continuous, then it is not differentiable."

  • C = "The function is continuous"
  • D = "The function is differentiable"

Statement 2 — Mother to son: "If you don't do your homework, then you can't watch TV."

  • H = "Do your homework"
  • T = "Can watch TV"

Which of the following pairs of propositions are logically equivalent? (Select all that apply)

  1. (¬C → ¬D) and (D → C)
  2. (¬H → ¬T) and (H → T)
  3. (H ↔ T) and (H → T) ∧ (T → H)
  4. (¬C → ¬D) and (C → D)
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
• p = "Roses are red"
  • q = "Violets are blue"

The statement "It is not true that roses are red and violets are blue" is logically equivalent to which of the following English sentences ?

  1. Roses are not red and violets are not blue
  2. Roses are not red or violets are not blue
  3. It is not true that roses are red or violets are blue
  4. Roses are not red and violets are blue
